data.text: Pizza Co. turns $100M of EBITDA into $50M of free cash flow a year after $30M of capex and $20M of interest. It carries $400M of debt against $100M of cash, which puts leverage at 4.0x and interest coverage at 5.0x.
The credit agreement caps leverage at 5.00x and requires interest coverage of at least 2.00x. At 4.0x and 5.0x, Pizza Co. passes both rules today.

Lend. This business throws off $50M of free cash flow a year and covers its interest 5.0x over. Leverage of 4.0x leaves a full turn of headroom under the 5.00x cap, so earnings could fall 20% before a rule is even tested.

Don't lend. The whole $400M comes due at once in 2028, and four years of free cash flow only adds about $200M. Even counting the $100M already in the bank, that is $300M against a $400M bill, with no revolver to bridge the gap. Repayment depends on a refinancing we don't control.

Both loan rules pass with room to spare: 4.0x leverage against a 5.00x cap and 5.0x coverage against a 2.00x floor. The Bear is right that 2028 needs a refinancing, but a borrower with this cash flow and headroom should be able to get one. The committee votes to lend.
Lend. Pizza Co. passes both loan rules with headroom and generates $50M of free cash flow a year. Watch the 2028 maturity: $400M due against about $300M of cash means it will need to refinance.
